newsitem.title: UK: Land Secs gains as rate outlook brightens.
newsitem.headline: Land Secs gains as rate outlook brightens.

text.p: Shares in Land Securities Plc and other top UK property stocks leapt on Wednesday, benefitting from the improved interest rate outlook after Tuesday's move to give the Bank of England freedom to set rates, dealers said.

Land Securities shares were up 15-1/2p at 830-1/2 by 0957 GMT, British Land Plc was up 10-1/2p at 599-1/2, Great Portland Estates Plc was up 6-1/2p at 212-1/2, Slough Estates Plc was up 4-1/2p at 323-1/2 and MEPC Plc was up 10p at 472-1/2.
Analyst Nan Rodgers at Charterhouse Tilney pointed out that gilt yields had fallen sharply after the new Labour government's Bank of England move, making property returns relatively more attractive.

She added that some property companies expect Labour to be more relaxed on granting planning consents than the outgoing Conservatives. "The feeling is that Labour could be more likely to take a pragmatic view," Rodgers said.

Separately analysts at BZW repeated an "overweight" stance on the sector, pointing out that real rental growth had reappeared for the first time this decade, dealers said. Analysts at BZW were not immediately available for comment.

Dealers said BZW argued there was "still value around" in the sector and highlighted MEPC, Great Portland, Greycoat Plc and Capital and Regional Plc among larger stocks in the sector, but was cautious on Land Securities and British Land.
